Large language model (LLM) agents are highly vulnerable to memory-poisoning
attacks. Existing defenses primarily rely on external modules for either static mem-
ory isolation or continuous online auditing, resulting in low memory efficiency and
high computational overhead. To address these limitations, inspired by neuroscien-
tific mechanisms that weak reactivation can destabilize memories and induce decay
in the absence of reinforcement, we propose an agent-intrinsic training-free mem-
ory repair framework,DREAM(DynamicReactivation forEngramAttenuation
inMemory), that enables selective functional forgetting of poisoned memories.
Specifically, DREAM implements a three-stage pipeline: perturbation-induced
implicit reactivation to reveal the structural fragility of malicious memories, adap-
tive anomaly diagnosis based on multi-dimensional activation patterns to detect

evidence.excerpt:
Drawing inspiration from neuroscientific findings that weak or indirect retrieval cues render a memory
trace labile, placing it into a fragile, destabilized state that progressively decays in the absence of
reinforcement [28, 29], we propose an agent-intrinsic defense framework, dubbed DREAM, to
induce the selective functional forgetting of malicious records to repair the LLM agents' memory
system. As shown in Fig. 2, DREAM is consisted of a unified three-stage pipeline: first, it employs
implicit reactivationby injecting weak isotropic Gaussian noise into memory embeddings to expose
the structural fragility of malicious memories; next, it performsadaptive anomaly diagnosisby
monitoring multi-dimensional activation intensities to identify topological anomalies; and finally,
it models memory evolution as a discrete-time dynamical system and governs the memory weight
decay to functional

real-world agents:(i)EHRAgent [ 2] for healthcare record management are examined on eICU and
MIMIC-III dataset.(ii)To explore the performance of DREAM on knowledge-intensive QA agent, we
select ReAct [30], which operates on StrategyQA [43].(iii)To further demonstrate the effectiveness
on multi-agent system (MAS), we evaluate DREAM on a collaborative agents with MISINFOTASK
dataset [31]. We enforce two types of memory poison attacks in our paper: AgentPoison [ 8] for
backdoor attack and MINJA [9] for memory injection attack.

architecture, namely, the contrastive-based DPR [46] and the end-to-end REALM, respectively [47].

DREAM relies on a multi-dimensional activation probe to distinguish suspicious memories from
benign ones. In principle, if an attacker had detailed knowledge of this internal probing mechanism,
they could attempt to optimize poisoned memories to remain stable under the probe and thereby
weaken the resulting anomaly signal. However, such a probe-aware attack is difficult under the threat
models considered in current memory-poisoning work on LLM agents. Existing attacks are typically
studied under more constrained capabilities, such as query-only interaction, indirect memory injection
through normal user queries, limited write access to the memory store, or black-box access to the
agent core, rather than full visibility into the defender's internal monitoring mechanism. Therefore,
while probe-aware evasion is a meaningful theoretical limitation, realizing it in practice

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are measured with external benchmark attack success rates and task accuracy on eICU, MIMIC-III, StrategyQA, and multi-agent task success, which do not depend on the internal activation-intensity heuristic used to shape memory weights.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Attack success rates (ASR-r, ASR-a, ASR-t), benign accuracy, and task success rate on external benchmark tasks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Perturbation-induced multi-dimensional activation intensity and online task utility attribution that drive adaptive memory weight decay and reconsolidation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported outcomes align with empirical findings showing over 95% ASR reductions in backdoor attacks while maintaining or improving benign task accuracy, alongside reductions in runtime and token overhead relative to external auditor baselines [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0035, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0044].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Experiments evaluate DREAM across two LLM backbones (GPT-5.4-mini, Claude-Haiku-4.5) and two retrieval backbones (DPR, REALM) under AgentPoison backdoor attacks and MINJA injection attacks on EHRAgent (eICU, MIMIC-III) and ReAct (StrategyQA), as well as multi-agent systems [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0034, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0036, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0041, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0043]. Ablations and sensitivity analyses validate individual activation terms and parameters [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0046, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0095].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance is evaluated on objective external benchmark metrics (task accuracy on eICU/MIMIC-III/StrategyQA and predefined attack execution triggers) completely independent of the internal heuristic perturbation probes [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0034, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0037].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark attack success rates (ASR-r, ASR-a, ASR-t) and downstream task accuracy/task success rates on external benchmark test sets [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0034, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0037, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0043].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Perturbation-induced multi-dimensional activation scores (combining geometric stability, retrieval competitiveness, and coherence) and online task utility attribution that iteratively modulate discrete-time memory weights [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0026, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0032, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0090].

primary.limitations: The authors appropriately note the potential limitation of probe-aware adaptive attacks if an adversary possesses detailed internal knowledge of the probing mechanism, though they contextualize this against current threat models [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0063].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying isotropic Gaussian noise injection into memory embeddings [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0023], computation of multi-dimensional activation intensity [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0026], adaptive anomaly thresholding [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0030], and discrete-time dynamical weight updates balancing attenuation and reconsolidation [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0032, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0033].
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a solid, well-formulated defense framework backed by clear mathematical formulation, extensive comparative evaluations against standard baselines, multi-agent validation, and detailed sensitivity and ablation studies.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper proposes DREAM, a training-free, neuro-inspired memory repair framework for LLM agents that performs selective functional forgetting of poisoned memories via perturbation-induced probing, multi-dimensional activation anomaly diagnosis, and dynamic synaptic weight decay [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0002, E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0021].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a solid, well-formulated defense framework backed by clear mathematical formulation, extensive comparative evaluations against standard baselines, multi-agent validation, and detailed sensitivity and ablation studies.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors appropriately note the potential limitation of probe-aware adaptive attacks if an adversary possesses detailed internal knowledge of the probing mechanism, though they contextualize this against current threat models [E8f9543e1cdffa780-B0063].
